Logged in as testfree-mar@elitescout.com, uploaded /tmp/test-video.webm (transcoded from /app/frontend/public/test-video.mp4 because Playwright's bundled Chromium cannot decode H.264 – the mp4 hit MediaError code 4 'SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED' and the marker studio could not open — this is a well-known headless-Chromium codec limitation, NOT an app bug), locked onto the player through ScoutMode's 10-tap flow (3 taps confirmed → Finish Early), filled Mikkel / age 12 / Winger / description, and submitted. ui_bugs.issue: When clicked during the analyzing phase, the overlay does close and setSubmitting(false) fires, BUT the page does NOT navigate to /dashboard — it stays on /upload with the plain upload form visible again. The subsequent /api/reports/{id}/status polls that fire from the browser after the click return 401 'Not authenticated' (auth cookie appears lost from the browser context immediately after the click). No background-analysis tracker element is present on the resulting page. Repro: log in as testfree-mar@elitescout.com → /upload → complete a full upload → within ~6s of the overlay appearing click wait-go-dashboard-btn. Expected: toast + navigate('/dashboard') + floating BackgroundAnalysisTracker visible; Actual: overlay closes, still on /upload, no tracker, 401s from status poll. RCA hypothesis: onContinueInBackground sets backgroundedRef.current=true but by the time the next poll tick fires, either (a) startBackgroundAnalysis() is throwing (silently) and short-circuiting the navigate() call, or (b) axios interceptor is invalidating the auth cookie on the first 401 during a mid-flight poll — worth logging both paths in the poll loop in UploadPage.jsx lines 462-506.

action_items: HIGH: Investigate why clicking wait-go-dashboard-btn does not navigate to /dashboard. The overlay closes (submitting becomes false) but React Router navigate('/dashboard') never lands, and status polls that immediately follow return 401. Suspect either startBackgroundAnalysis(data.id) throwing/swallowing the error before the navigate() call in UploadPage.jsx (~lines 464-472), or a race where backgroundedRef.current is read before the ref update propagates on the very first poll tick. Add a console.log('background-handoff', data.id) around startBackgroundAnalysis and a try/catch to surface any thrown error.

MINOR: In headless Chromium environments, the app's marker studio silently sits in a videoReady=false state (video.error.code=4, videoWidth=0) because Playwright's Chromium build cannot decode H.264 mp4. Not a code bug — but consider adding a visible user-facing warning banner inside MarkerStudio when video.error !== null AND videoReady stays false for >5s, so live users on unsupported browsers get an actionable error rather than a permanently-disabled Review button.
critical_code_review_comments: PrecisionScanOverlay.jsx (415 lines) is clean, focused, and well-commented. visualStageFor / STAGE_PCT / STAGE_TAU cleanly encode the backend-driven mapping and the maxPctRef guarantees monotonicity — verified live (22% → 33% as backend_step advanced 1→2). Good separation between uploading / analyzing / done phases.

The overlay correctly wires playerName, playerAge, playerPosition, tapsCount and heroImage from UploadPage props (verified: chips show 'MIKKEL', 'U12 • WINGER', row 2 shows '3/3 taps verified'). No stale-props issues observed.
Hero card is created from a blob: URL of the user's marker frame (naturalWidth=480, naturalHeight=848 decoded live) — spec fully met.
SCOUT TIP background image /assets/scout-tip.jpg loads with naturalWidth=1024 (>0) — spec met.
Row 2 subtitle correctly interpolates the real tapsCount from markerAnchors.length in UploadPage.jsx line 591 — no client-side lie.
Zero console errors observed while the overlay was open — good UX quality.

One rough edge: onContinueInBackground handoff in UploadPage.jsx (~line 593-598) merely sets backgroundedRef.current=true and relies on the next poll tick to observe it. If the user clicks after the poll loop has ALREADY returned (e.g., upload completed quickly and we already went to done/hero), the flag becomes a no-op. Not a blocker for the current UI verification but relates to the HIGH action item above.
The DoneScreen at the bottom of PrecisionScanOverlay.jsx (lines 362-415) is unchanged from earlier user-approved iterations — code-reviewed only.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The full E2E flow can be repeated by (a) transcoding /app/frontend/public/test-video.mp4 → /tmp/test-video.webm using `ffmpeg -i /tmp/test-video.mp4 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -b:v 500k -c:a libopus -t 15 /tmp/test-video.webm -y` (Playwright Chromium cannot decode H.264 mp4 → video.error.code=4 → marker studio permanently disabled), (b) uploading webm which then triggers ScoutMode (10-tap) not MANUAL mode, (c) tapping the video stage 3 times, clicking 'scout-confirm-mark' after each tap, then clicking 'scout-finish-early'. Description field (data-testid='upload-player-description') is REQUIRED. After submit, the overlay appears within 5–10 s. The 'Go to Dashboard' navigation bug is reproducible — click the button 5–10 s after overlay appears, observe that URL stays on /upload and that /api/reports/{id}/status requests return 401.
rca_of_the_issue: GO TO DASHBOARD click does not lead to /dashboard. The button correctly invokes onContinueInBackground → backgroundedRef.current = true, but the subsequent path inside the poll while-loop (UploadPage.jsx lines 464-472) is either silently throwing inside startBackgroundAnalysis(data.id) before reaching navigate('/dashboard'), or the branch is not entered because of a race between the ref update and the loop's next tick. The 401s on /api/reports/{id}/status that follow the click are a symptom: the axios instance evidently loses its httpOnly-cookie context (possibly because startBackgroundAnalysis constructs a fresh api client that isn't wired with `withCredentials: true`, or because navigate() was never called so the loop keeps polling on the still-mounted UploadPage but with a cleared session). Recommended fix path: (1) wrap startBackgroundAnalysis in try/catch and console.error the failure, (2) always call navigate('/dashboard') AFTER startBackgroundAnalysis regardless of its outcome, (3) verify the axios client used by startBackgroundAnalysis honours `withCredentials: true` — the same axios instance that succeeded on the upload POST should be reused.
